title: The Impact of Large-Scale Free Prescription Glasses Distribution on the Academic Achievement of Children
abstract: This working paper evaluates the academic effects of distributing prescription eyeglasses at large scale to children in Mexico. The analysis uses administrative grade records covering approximately 5.5 million students and compares achievement patterns around program exposure. The estimates indicate a moderate improvement in grades, with larger gains among underserved students and children with more serious vision impairment. The paper also assesses the program as a cost-effective way to improve educational outcomes, highlighting how correcting an unmet vision need can support learning at scale.
